payload.title: Uniform time sampling with Pyleoclim
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook demonstrates methods for placing paleoclimate records on a uniform time axis using the Pyleoclim library. It addresses the common issue of uneven time spacing in paleosciences by exploring interpolation, binning, resampling, and Gaussian kernel coarsening techniques. The notebook uses data from Jouzel et al. (2007) and provides visualizations to compare the effectiveness of each method. The goal is to familiarize users with time regridding methods in Pyleoclim.
goals: Become familiar with time regridding methods in Pyleoclim

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduction to the issue of uneven time spacing in paleosciences and the use of Pyleoclim for uniform time sampling.
section_blurbs.heading: Uniform time sampling with Pyleoclim

section_blurbs.blurb: Overview of the notebook's purpose, goals, and relevant packages, including the introduction of the EDC-dD dataset.

section_blurbs.heading: An uneven resolution

section_blurbs.blurb: Explanation and implementation of interpolation methods to project data onto an evenly spaced time axis.
section_blurbs.heading: Solution 1: Interpolation

section_blurbs.blurb: Description of binning as an alternative to interpolation, averaging series values over uniform bins.
section_blurbs.heading: Solution 2: Binning

section_blurbs.blurb: Use of the pandas resampler to aggregate data, demonstrated with averaging over a 5ka interval.
section_blurbs.heading: Solution 3: Resampling

section_blurbs.heading: Solution 4: Coarsening with a Gaussian kernel

section_blurbs.blurb: Comparison of all methods on a 5ka grid, highlighting differences in smoothness and jerkiness.
section_blurbs.heading: Battle Royale

section_blurbs.heading: Summary
